hypothesis: Reading the INT8 dense matrices from canonical.qc, converted once by qwen36-canonical, instead of converting them at every start shortens the start and lowers the peak memory footprint, with the same logits and the same speed; the peak resident set rises a little while the file's pages are mapped.
model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration) converted to Colibri's qwen36 container: INT4 routed experts with gs=64 group scales, f16 dense weights (quantized to INT8 at load) and f16 embedding; 23 GB of safetensors; canonical.qc beside it (1.94 GB, written on 2026-10-01 by an earlier version of the tool and byte-identical to the file the tool of 2026-10-05 wrote; on the tiny fixture this branch's tool writes the same file as that one)
command: for each version, git archive <its commit> c | tar -x -C <dir>, then from the repository root, with the flags of make -C c qwen36: clang -O3 -Xclang -fopenmp -I<libomp>/include -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-unused-function -I<dir>/c docs/experiments/qwen36-canonical-dense-2026-10-07/bench.c -o <dir>/qwen36-bench -lm -L<libomp>/lib -lomp; every run: /usr/bin/time -l env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$HOME SNAP=<model> <dir>/qwen36-bench promessi_sposi.txt 64,512 32; baseline = 0d5eae65 (the embedding change this branch is stacked on), trial = ac9c4c83 (a local commit not in the repository) with canonical.qc beside the model (written on 2026-10-01 by an earlier version of the tool, byte-identical to the one the tool of 2026-10-05 wrote); 1485d769 is the measured ac9c4c83 with changes to how the file is used, made after a review: it is used in a VK=1 or CUDA build that runs on the CPU, a file beside the model that does not match is set aside and the matrices are converted, the list of matrices follows the loader for the other geometries, names under the language_model. prefix are read, the log line says the matrices were read from the file, the file is closed as soon as they are copied and an empty QWEN_DENSE_CACHE is unset. Besides, the tool's writer is a function the new test calls, it syncs the file before the rename, and the docs, a CI step and the commit message changed. It is rebased onto the embedding change as sent, which differs from the measured 0d5eae65 by four small changes to how the embedding is loaded (see its record). On the tiny fixture its layer outputs and logits are dev's, byte for byte, with and without the file, and its tool writes the same file as before. Rebased onto dev 1509ea5b: the harness compiles to the same code section on the M1 from dev 1509ea5b as from dev 94dee9d2, from 1485d769 as from b03809d3 (a local commit, the code commit before the rebase), and, for the embedding change under it, from 2633451f as from 71d56e35 (local too; its record says how 71d56e35 relates to the measured 0d5eae65)

hardware.cpu: Apple M1, 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores (MacBook Air, MacBookAir10,1, no fan)

config.BUILD: flags of make -C c qwen36 on macOS: clang -O3 -Xclang -fopenmp, no -mcpu, no METAL
config.EXPERT_CACHE: 16 experts per layer, set by the harness (qwen36's default until dev sized the cache from the RAM, which the harness does not use)
config.PROMPT: the first 64 and the first 512 tokens of promessi_sposi.txt (speed-bench/promessi_sposi.txt of antirez's ds4 at commit 0aaea5a, of which the harness reads the first 20,480 bytes; prompt_hash is its SHA-256), each from an empty state; after each, 32 greedy tokens
config.ORDER: 1 warm-up run (baseline, discarded), then baseline trial trial baseline baseline trial trial baseline, one process each
config.REST: thermal state nominal, then 60 s, before every run
config.DENSE_WEIGHTS: converted to INT8 at every start (0d5eae65, the embedding change alone)
config.MEASURED: tokens per second of the 32 tokens generated after the 512-token prompt (the first token excluded)
